requirement:
`languages::Rust` implements `OutlineLang` under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider`. Its default value is
cheaply cloneable and claims `.rs`. Filename-based constructors select it under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`.
rationale:
The reviewed test adequately checks `requirements.sdk.sources.rust.language`. I did not request implementation source.

**Obligations derived from the subject:**
1. `languages::Rust` implements `OutlineLang`, which supplies a name, claimed extensions and an outline operation.
2. Its default value is cheaply cloneable.
3. It claims `.rs`.
4. Filename-based constructors select it. The cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults` adds that extension matching is case-insensitive.

**Test:** `crates/trust-but-verify/tests/outline_content.rs#fn[bundled_languages_claim_extensions_and_supply_the_same_public_outline]` is marked `{test}` for this requirement. Its generic `check` helper is called with `languages::Rust`, filename `a.RS` and source `fn check() {}`.

| Obligation | How the test covers it |
|---|---|
| Implements `OutlineLang` | `check` is bounded by `L: OutlineLang + Default + Copy`, so the call only compiles if `Rust` implements the trait. The test asserts `name()` is non-empty and `extensions()` equals `["rs"]`. It builds an outline through `OutlineContent::from_source_with(&language, ...)` and checks the selector `fn[check]`, the root span, and that spans lie within the source. It also calls `search_structure`. |
| Default value | `L::default().fingerprint_scheme()` is asserted equal to `"rust-structural-v1"`. |
| Cheaply cloneable | `size_of::<L>() == 0` rules out an owned allocation. `Clone::clone` is called and the clone's extensions are asserted. |
| Claims `.rs` | `extensions()` is asserted equal to `["rs"]` exactly. |
| Filename-based constructors select it | `OutlineContent::from_source("a.RS", ...)` gives the same fingerprint, scheme and selectable `fn[check]` as the explicit `Rust` path. This covers inference and case-insensitivity. The loop over claimed extensions uses an uppercase `not-present.RS` and confirms the same fingerprint and selection. |

The plain-text fallback is only partly covered here. The test asserts `PlainText` has an empty extension list and the name `plain-text`. That fallback belongs to the cited `requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`, which is context and not the subject. The outline and language-provider semantics are likewise cited context.

I found no plausible behavior that violates the subject and would pass this test. A non-claiming `.rs`, a wrong default, a heap-owning clone, or a failure to select `Rust` for `.RS` would each fail an assertion.

text: :::{req} language
`languages::Rust` implements `OutlineLang` under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.language_provider`. Its default value is
cheaply cloneable and claims `.rs`. Filename-based constructors select it under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.defaults`.
:::{req} language_provider
`OutlineLang` defines the language interface. Each implementation supplies its
name, claimed extensions, and outlining operation. Cloning a language shares
its prepared configuration instead of rebuilding it or copying it in proportion
to its size. Its result uses the public items, spans, and hashes under
{cite}`requirements.sdk.outlines.items`.
```rust,ignore
pub trait OutlineLang: Clone + Send + Sync {
/// Stable name of this language implementation.
fn name(&self) -> &str;
/// Claimed filename extensions, without their leading dots.
fn extensions(&self) -> &[&str];
/// Interpret supplied text into selectable items and structural hashes.
fn outline(&self, source: &str) -> Result<Outline, OutlineError>;
:::{req} defaults
The filename-based constructors include Rust, Python, TypeScript, TSX,
Markdown, CSS, TOML, and YAML languages. Extension matching is
case-insensitive, using each implementation's claimed extensions.
The [language chapters](#language-specific-rules) define those mappings.
A filename without a claimed extension uses the
[plain-text outline](sources/plain-text.md): a file root with one child per
nonblank line.
